Subject: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist + eval plan

Hi Alice / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Short recap + next steps below. I attached a one-page model shortlist and the prompt sets we discussed.

Quick recap from our side:
- Use case: customer-facing summarization + semantic search augmentation for support articles (safety + low hallucination priority).
- Key non-negotiables: p95 latency <= 250ms on 512-token responses; hallucination rate < 3% on the eval set; token-cost sensitivity for 20M tokens/mo.

Recommended shortlist (high-level rationale):
1) redwood-3.5-q4 (quantized) — Best cost/latency balance for production inference. Expected p95 ~80-120ms (512 tokens) on our dedicated nodes, strong instruction-following; lowest unit cost when quantized.
2) flan-ul2-xxl — Strong instruction-following and few-shot performance; higher compute but better at complex summarization that reduces downstream hallucinations. Good candidate for quality-critical routes.
3) open-70b-refined — Highest quality on abstractive summarization benchmarks we ran (see attached CSV), but ~2-3x cost vs redwood-3.5 and higher p95. Good as a fall-back for escalations/long-form responses.

Attachments included: redwood-model-shortlist.pdf (one-pager), acme-benchmark-results.csv (pilot run), acme-prompt-sets.zip (candidate prompts + scoring rubric).

Proposed eval plan / next steps:
- We (Redwood) run the pilot harness on a 2-week eval set you provide (we can use the sample prompts in the attached ZIP) and share: latency p50/p95, token cost estimates, hallucination rate, and qualitative examples.
- You share a representative eval set (50-200 samples) and any blocked terms / safety constraints by EOD Thu, Jun 12.
- Follow-up call to review results and align on pilot configuration: Tue, Jun 16 or Wed, Jun 17.

Can you confirm the eval timeline and whether you want a dedicated pilot capacity quote (we can provide committed GPU hours for the 2-week test)?

Thanks — I’ve looped in Neha (SE) and Rishi (AE) to help with technical questions and costing.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — quick answers to your questions: 

1) Latency numbers: the p95 ~80-120ms quoted for redwood-3.5-q4 are on our Dedicated nodes configured with T4x2 equivalents in us-east-1 and using our continuous batching + KV caching enabled (512-token responses, 16-token prompt average). On Hosted the numbers can be slightly higher depending on multi-tenant load; for the pilot we recommend Dedicated pilot capacity (isolated) to guarantee p95.

2) Data residency: yes — pilot can be provisioned in us-east-1; logs/audit trails will remain in your VPC bucket. We’ll provide an exportable audit log (S3 export) at the end of the pilot.

3) Ballpark cost: for a 2-week pilot scaled to ~20M tokens/month equivalent (pro-rata ~2.3M tokens for the test window), approximate token cost estimates (incl. serving infra + I/O):
   - redwood-3.5-q4 (quantized): ~$900-1,200 for the pilot window
   - flan-ul2-xxl: ~$2,200-2,800
   - open-70b-refined: ~$3,800-5,200
Exact numbers depend on request distribution and caching hits; we’ll provide a per-route estimate once we have the eval samples.

Suggested metrics for the pilot: latency (p50/p95), token cost, hallucination rate (manual adjudication on a 50-sample subset), relevance/ROUGE-style scores, and end-to-end perceived usefulness (stakeholder survey).

I’ve also uploaded the pilot harness URL and the scoring rubric to the Drive folder (link in the email metadata).

If you’re OK we’ll provision a small Dedicated pilot for 2 weeks in us-east-1 and run all three models against your sample set. We’ll then recommend a primary production model and a fallback.

— Neha

Primary suggestion for pilot: redwood-3.5-q4 — production-first balance (cost + latency).
Quality fallback (for critical responses): open-70b-refined — use via routing policy for escalations / long-form summarization.
